Trident shares rally 13% after Q2-profit surges 93%, company announces Rs 4,650 crore capex plan; check target price
sum: Shares of Trident rallied as much as 13.4 percent to hit an intra-day high of Rs 25.18 on the BSE on Tuesday after the textile fabric manufacturer reported a 93 percent increase in net profit during the July-September quarter of the financial year 2026-27 and announced a Rs 4,650 crore capacity expansion and modernisation plan. The proposed capital expenditure is nearly one-third of the company’s overall market capitalisation of just over Rs 12,500 crore.

Trident shares opened at Rs 23.11 and surged 13.4 percent to hit an intra-day high of Rs 25.18 from the previous closing of Rs 22.20. However, the stock pared most of its early gains during the session. At around 1.05 pm, the stock was trading 5.95 per cent higher at Rs 23.45.

Trident Ltd reported a 93.1 percent year-on-year increase in consolidated profit attributable to owners of the company to Rs 175.5 crore for the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27 (Q2FY27), compared with Rs 90.9 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous financial year.
The company’s revenue from operations declined 3.8 percent to Rs 1,719.48 crore in September quarter from Rs 1,787.17 crore in the year-ago period.

Despite the decline in revenue, Trident reported a strong improvement in operating performance, with earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) rising 46.5 percent YoY to Rs 313.7 crore from Rs 214.1 crore in Q2 FY26.
EBITDA margin improved significantly to 18 percent in the September quarter, compared with 12 percent in the corresponding quarter last year, marking an expansion of 600 basis points.

On a sequential basis, profit attributable to owners increase 11.1 percent in Q2 FY27 from Rs 158.09 crore in Q1 FY27. Revenue declined 3.8 percent in the quarter under review against Rs 1,786.83 crore in the year-ago period, while total expenses fell 4.9 percent.

2 dividend stocks to target a £1,326 income from a £20k Stocks and Shares ISA
sum: A Stocks and Shares ISA makes a brilliant home for dividend-paying UK shares. All shareholder payouts are tax-free, whether you reinvest them or draw them as income.

The good news is that plenty of FTSE 100 and FTSE 250 stocks offer attractive yields of 5%, 6% and in some cases more than 7%. With luck, that income should steadily rise as you reinvest dividends and companies increase payouts.
Nothing is guaranteed in investing, but I think these two FTSE 100 dividend stars are worth considering for an income portfolio today.
I've done brilliantly from wealth manager M&G (LSE: M&G). Its shares are up 20% over 12 months and 58% over five years, with dividends on top.

When I bought them, they yielded a stunning 10%. Such a dizzying yield can be a warning sign, but I believed it was sustainable. So far, I've been proved right. However, as the shares have climbed, the yield has slipped to 6.63% for new buyers. Still generous though. The board is also targeting annual dividend growth of around 2%. Although right now, that's below inflation.
In the first half of 2026, M&G's adjusted operating profit rose a solid 15% to £435m, driven by stronger asset-management revenues and growth in its life insurance business.

There are risks. A stock market crash could discourage customers from investing and reduce the commission-based fees M&G earns. It also operates in fiercely competitive markets, and is currently fighting a battle royale to win bulk annuity business from pension schemes. Passive tracker funds remain a constant challenge to its active management model.

Did The Market Read Target Stock Right?
sum: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Investors who purchased Target (TGT) shares on October 20, 2025 saw a 75.1% return a year later, compared with a 15.8% gain for the S&P 500. Over that year, the retailer’s sales went from shrinking to growing. On August 19, 2026, management raised its sales outlook following a quarter helped by a tariff refund. So are more shoppers really walking into Target, and is its profit higher without that refund?

So far, yes: Target is growing because more people shop there, not because they pay more. Revenue fell 1.6% from a year earlier in the quarter ended November 1, 2025. By the quarter ended May 2, 2026, revenue was growing at 6.7%, and the quarter ended August 1, 2026, delivered 5.3% growth.

Management said comparable sales rose 3.8% in that latest quarter, driven by a 3.6% increase in traffic, with the average ticket about flat. On the August 19 call, management raised its full-year sales growth guidance to around 5%, one percentage point above its prior outlook. Over the exact dates of Target’s rise, Walmart and Costco Wholesale returned 11.0% and 6.9%, so Target’s shares did not simply move with its rivals.
Moves like this test every retirement plan. If your advisor recently retired, it is a good moment for a free second opinion from our partner firm.

Most of it: management said tariff refunds supplied 3.7 of the 4.7 percentage points Target added to its gross margin in the quarter ended August 1, 2026. Those refunds provided a $994 million pretax benefit, recorded as a reduction of cost of sales. Target’s operating margin for that quarter was 9.6%, compared with 5.2% a year earlier.

Target’s profit is still higher without the refund, but by a much smaller amount. Excluding the refund leaves operating income at about $1.57 billion for that quarter, compared with $1.32 billion a year earlier. Management expects its full-year operating margin, excluding tariff refunds, to land around 0.5 percentage point above last year’s adjusted rate.

Alvotech Shares Rise 5.6% After Barclays Upgrades Rating and Doubles Price Target
sum: Alvotech (NASDAQ:ALVO) shares gained 5.6% in premarket trading after Barclays upgraded the biosimilar drug developer from Underweight to Overweight and raised its price target from $4.00 to $8.00.
The bank cited changes in Alvotech's regulatory outlook following the conclusion of a US Food and Drug Administration inspection at the company's manufacturing facility in Reykjavik, Iceland.
The upgrade reverses Barclays' previous assessment of the company, which had included concerns about debt levels and capital expenditure commitments.
Barclays highlighted the FDA's decision to close its May 2026 inspection of Alvotech's Reykjavik manufacturing facility with a Voluntary Action Indicated (VAI) classification.
A VAI classification means the agency identified conditions that may warrant voluntary corrective action but does not currently intend to pursue regulatory or administrative enforcement.
The inspection outcome was a central factor in Barclays' revised assessment of Alvotech's regulatory position.
Following the inspection, Alvotech resubmitted biologics licence applications in June for proposed biosimilars referencing Simponi, Eylea and Prolia/Xgeva.

Target Stock Is Up 60% in 2026. Wall Street’s Average Target Now Sits Below It
sum: Now Live: Discover how much upside your favorite stocks could have using TIKR’s new Valuation Model (It’s free) >>>

Target Corporation (TGT) closed at $165.44 on August 21, a fresh 52-week high, after second-quarter earnings on August 19 beat on nearly every line and set off a wave of analyst price-target hikes. Here is the detail that run obscures: even after all those raises, the average Wall Street target sits at around $162, below where the stock now trades. The print itself drew a muted first-day reaction, and the rally only found its legs two sessions later. For a buyer today, that frames the real question. After a run that has lifted the stock roughly 60% this year, how much is left?
The Beat Was Real, but $1.65 of It Came From a Tariff Refund

The turnaround itself is not in question, and TIKR has walked through the traffic-led recovery that got the stock here. What Q2 added was a wrinkle in earnings quality. Reported EPS of $4.11 doubled from $2.05, but that figure included a $1.65-per-share benefit from a $994 million pretax refund of IEEPA tariffs, booked as a reduction of cost of sales. Strip it out, and adjusted EPS grew about 20%, still strong, but a different result from “earnings doubled.” The same caveat runs through the gross margin of 33.7%, which expanded 4.7 points, with 3.7 of those coming from the refund.

Underneath the one-time boost, the operating story held: net sales rose 5.3% to $26.5 billion on a 3.8% comp, and management raised full-year guidance to around 5% sales growth. CFO Jim Lee steered investors away from the headline himself, noting adjusted EPS excluding refunds “were up 20% versus prior year,” and calling that “the number we probably want everyone to anchor on to grow off of going forward.”
See historical and forward estimates for Target stock (It’s free!) >>>

Target trades at roughly 17 times trailing earnings and 17.8 times NTM earnings, up from the roughly 11 to 13 times range it carried through late 2025 and early 2026. On EV/EBITDA, the trailing multiple has climbed to 10.3x from under 7x at the start of the year. At 11x, investors were paid to wait through an uncertain recovery. At 17x, they are paying up for one that still has to finish.

Target vs. Walmart: Which Retail Stock Is the Better Buy After Q2 Earnings?
sum: Retail giants Target TGT) and Walmart WMT) both topped Q2 earnings expectations this week and raised their full-year outlooks, but investors reacted very differently.

Target's turnaround gained further credibility following accelerating sales and traffic growth, while Walmart shares tumbled after softer-than-expected U.S. comparable sales and cautious near-term guidance overshadowed an otherwise solid quarter.
With that in mind, let's compare their latest results, valuations, and dividends to determine which stock offers the more attractive investment opportunity.
Target delivered one of its strongest reports in several quarters, with Q2 sales rising more than 5% year over year to $26.53 billion and topping estimates of $26.12 billion.

Comparable sales increased nearly 4%. Importantly, the improvement was largely traffic-driven, with comparable traffic rising 3.6%. Digital comparable sales increased 8.7%, fueled by more than 25% growth in same-day delivery.

On the bottom line, Target's Q2 adjusted net income was $1.88 billion, including a $752 million tariff refund. Excluding the refund, this equated to adjusted earnings of $2.46 per share, up 20% YoY and comfortably exceeding expectations of $2.30.
When including the tariff refund, Target's Q2 adjusted EPS more than doubled to $4.11.

sum: Stronger quarterly execution, stable guidance, digital convenience, and disciplined merchandising have brought renewed attention to a major retailer navigating cautious demand and intense competition.

Target Corporation (NYSE:TGT) Consumer Defensive Target Corporation (NYSE:TGT) 158.36 USD +0.410 0.260% Last Updated at: 2026-11-06T21:08:00Z , a major American general merchandise retailer, has returned to market focus after stronger quarterly results and an improved research assessment. The companys latest performance also places it within the broader S&P 500 conversation, where large consumer-facing businesses are being measured on demand resilience, operational discipline, and their ability to adapt to changing shopping habits. Targets recent update suggests that its combination of stores, digital services, owned brands, and everyday essentials is helping the retailer navigate a complicated consumer environment.

Targets latest quarter came in ahead of market expectations, supported by stronger revenue and better earnings performance. The result matters because large retailers continue facing cautious household spending, promotional pressure, and uneven demand across merchandise categories.

Target offers apparel, groceries, beauty products, electronics, home goods, household essentials, baby products, and pet supplies through its national store network and digital platform. This broad assortment allows the company to serve customers across both essential and discretionary needs.

The latest quarter suggests that Targets operating model is showing greater balance. Stronger performance indicates that customers remain engaged with the retailers product range, while management continues working to improve inventory levels, promotional planning, and store execution.

Target maintained its full-year earnings outlook following the quarterly update. Stable guidance can be meaningful when consumer stock conditions remain mixed because it signals that the company continues to see a manageable path through the remainder of the year.
The retailers outlook depends on several moving parts. Customer traffic, average transaction values, promotional activity, freight costs, wages, and product availability can all influence results.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley split on SpaceX stock price target
sum: Goldman Sachs set a $205 price target on SpaceX stock while Morgan Stanley set a $300 target, a gap that implies a roughly $1 trillion difference in valuation

A $205 price target came from Goldman Sachs, where a team led by Eric Sheridan handled coverage, while Adam Jonas led the Morgan Stanley team to a $300 figure, MarketWatch reported. Both firms initiated coverage with the equivalent of a buy rating. SpaceX stock closed Monday at $160.42.

The divergence between the two banks was not the only notable call to emerge Tuesday. Raymond James $RJF, another underwriter on the IPO, initiated coverage with an $800 price target and a strong buy rating, according to CNBC. In a note to clients, Gesuale wrote that Starship's ability to drive down the price of getting to orbit was central to the firm's thesis, calling SpaceX "one of the defining industrial infrastructure companies of the 21st Century." The $800 target represents a potential gain of roughly 399% from where shares finished Monday, and Raymond James contended that AI-driven products and services could represent an additional growth layer beyond the core launch business. A $225 price target and an outperform rating were issued by RBC Capital Markets when it opened coverage, Business Insider reported.

LSEG data cited by CNBC showed that buy and strong buy ratings accounted for roughly two-thirds of all analyst recommendations on SpaceX early Tuesday, with price targets clustered mostly in the $200-to-$250 range. Morgan Stanley's $300 target was an outlier on the high end among the IPO underwriters.

SpaceX joined the Nasdaq $NDAQ-100 Index before trading began Tuesday, becoming one of the first companies to benefit from the exchange's revised fast-track inclusion rules. The inclusion opened SpaceX stock to passive buying from funds and ETFs benchmarked to the index, which collectively commands more than $800 billion in assets globally.

SpaceX's June IPO priced shares at $135, raising $85.7 billion in proceeds — a record for the largest public offering ever. SpaceX reported a net loss of $4.94 billion in 2025 alongside revenue of $18.67 billion. The company also recorded a $4.28 billion loss in the first quarter of this year.

Stock market outlook: S&P 500 to lose much of 2026 gains as 'speculation is hitting extreme levels'
sum: The S&P 500 just notched its best quarter since 2020 and is up about 9% so far this year, but it’s mostly downhill from here, according to Bank of America.
In a note on Tuesday, analysts reaffirmed their year-end price target of 7,100 for the broad market index, representing a 5% drop from the week’s closing level.

“Our bear market signposts suggest speculation is hitting extreme levels as high multiple stocks have gapped up demonstrably, an event that has historically preceded a valuation ‘snapback,'” BofA said.

The bank added that S&P 500 companies are generating less free cash flow relative to net income compared to historical trends. That’s as so-called hyperscalers have seen their free cash flow plunge due to massive spending on the AI boom, eroding their earnings.

At the same time, the Federal Reserve is fighting sticky inflation after more than five years of letting it run above its 2% target. BofA recently predicted the Fed has now run out of patience and will hike rates three times this year to finally rein in inflation.
To be sure, the S&P 500 generally saw positive returns during previous tightening cycles, as stocks peaked six to 12 months after the first rate hike.
But Fed rate hikes now would hit differently, BofA explained, because the S&P 500 is more expensive ahead of a first rate hike than any other cycle, except for the one that ran from 1999 to 2000.
